name: Victorian Curriculum: Digital Technologies, Levels 7–10
note: Projects link to these topics (their "curriculum" list). Each topic describes, in plain words, the content it relates to in the Victorian Curriculum F–10 Version 2.0. Put the official content description code in "code" (from the VCAA website) and it shows beside the topic in Settings > Curriculum.

topics.text: How hardware components (such as sensors, actuators and microcontrollers) and software work together to make a digital system.
How data (numbers, text, sound and light) is represented in digital systems, including in binary.
Defining and breaking down a problem into smaller parts, with design criteria.
Designing algorithms with sequence, decisions (branching) and repetition (iteration), including nested control structures, and representing them as flowcharts or pseudocode.
Tracing algorithms to predict their output and find errors.
Implementing, modifying and debugging programs with control structures and functions in a general-purpose programming language (here, Arduino C++).
Designing how people interact with a digital system (the user experience).
Evaluating solutions against the design criteria.
How networked digital systems (such as WiFi) send and receive data, and how they can be kept secure.
Acquiring, storing and processing data from sensors, and checking it's accurate.
Designing algorithms with more complex decisions and repetition, and data structures such as arrays.
Validating algorithms and programs by tracing and testing them with test cases.
Implementing, modifying and debugging modular programs that use functions, libraries and data structures.
Evaluating solutions and their possible future impact, and how well they meet the needs of users.
